name: Runner Extras - TestPage Trigger Inject Timing
brief: Regression for issue #2411: a table-level DB-trigger subscriber (OnBeforeInsertEvent) on a precompiled Base App table was silently inert when that table's NCLMetaTable was first built through TestPageFactory.TryBuildBlankRecord -- the record-construction path shared by a directly-opened TestPage and by CodeunitPatches.NavFormHandle_CreateTarget (a plain `Page X` variable) -- rather than through one of the three sites #2412 already fixed (RecordPatches.CreateObjectInstance, RecordPatches.CreateObjectInstance.cs, NavRecordRefPatches.RecordRef.Open).
description:
#2412 fixed the ordering gap for a table whose NCLMetaTable is first built by a bare `Record X` variable or a `RecordRef.Open` call, by calling EventSubscriberPatches.InjectValidateSubsForTable + InjectTriggerSubsForTable at those three construction sites. Issue #2411 audited every OTHER call site that builds (or fetches, lazily building) an NCLMetaTable via RecordPatches.GetOrBuildNCLMetaTable / EnsureTableInMetadataCache, and found exactly one more that hands a live NavRecord to AL/test code without either injection pass: TestPageFactory.TryBuildBlankRecord, shared by TestPageFactory.TryBuild (a directly-opened TestPage) and CodeunitPatches.NavFormHandle_CreateTarget (a plain Page-variable's Rec). Every other candidate site audited in #2411 (RecordPatches.CompanySystemTable, RecordPatches.FieldFindIntercept / FieldVirtualTable FlowField source-table resolution, RecordPatches.InstallBaselineDisk, RecordPatches.NclMetadataCachePopulator's NCLMetadata_GetMetaTableById/GetMetaApplicationObjectByType, RecordPatches.TestDataHydration) only ever resolves an NCLMetaTable for bulk/raw DataAccessSource-level row operations or read-only metadata lookups -- none of them ever construct or hand back a live NavRecord instance a test could call Insert/Modify/Delete/Rename on, so those are out of scope for this fix.

IMPORTANT, measured during #2411's investigation (stack trace on EventSubscriberPatches.InjectTriggerSubsForTable, both with and without the TestPageFactory fix): the AL test in this suite does NOT discriminate the fix -- it is GREEN with TryBuildBlankRecord's injection calls removed too, and that was true for every precompiled Base App table tried (Resource/156, then Warehouse Employee/7301). The reason is structural, not table-specific: BC's own SetSourceTable -> EnsureMetadataLoaded -> InitializeFromMetadata, and separately NewRecordAsync -> RaiseOnNewRecordAsync -> NavRecord.get_OldRecord, ALREADY construct the table's xRec via NCLMetaTable.CreateObjectInstance (RecordPatches.CreateObjectInstance.cs) -- one of #2412's three already-fixed sites -- on every path where TestPageFactory.TryBuild/CodeunitPatches.NavFormHandle_CreateTarget successfully build a real compiled page object, and that happens before Insert/Modify/Delete/Rename can ever dispatch on the record TryBuildBlankRecord itself returned. So the subscriber is already wired (via xRec, onto the same shared per-table trigger handler) by the time the test's own Insert runs, with or without this issue's fix. The fix in TryBuildBlankRecord is still correct and still shipped -- it keeps this site's contract identical to the other three, and it is what would matter on RunnerPageInstance.TryCreate's record-only fallback (no page object built at all), which the runner does hit for other pages (see RunnerPageInstance's own catch block and 'no source-expression table' branch) but which could not be forced deterministically for this specific repro without an unreasonably fragile setup. This suite therefore stays as an end-to-end regression/contract test -- 'a table-level trigger subscriber on a table first touched via a TestPage does eventually fire' -- not as a RED/GREEN proof of the TryBuildBlankRecord diff; the diff's correctness rests on matching #2412's already-proven pattern at the other three sites plus the reasoning above, not on this AL suite. This suite is deliberately the only runner-extras bundle referencing Warehouse Employee (precompiled Base App table 7301).
